card.name: Pronoun after belief or claim verbs
card.fires_on: The word right after a verb of believing, thinking or calling (believe, thinking, called), usually a pronoun like they, he, their or himself that starts the believed claim. Seen in general web prose on politics, religion and misconceptions.

modes.label: Subject after believe
modes.description: A pronoun starts the clause that states what someone believes.
modes.example: The candidates and their political parties believe<< they>> must spend in excess of the legal limit

modes.label: Other claim openers
modes.description: A word that starts a stated claim or a contrast, such as a, as, or not.
modes.example: Newton's laws stood in direct opposition to the common misconception that a<< force>> is required to keep an object in motion

modes.label: Self-reference after verb
modes.description: A reflexive or possessive word follows a verb of calling or becoming.
modes.example: The baker, Vincent Fettmilch, who called<< himself>> the "New Haman", organized attacks

card.plain: It fires on the word that begins what someone believes or claims, like the "they" in "politicians believe they may...".
